answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn reputation-weighted rewards; the contract slashes that bond if a randomly selected task fails an auditable challenge. Creating a fake identity therefore does not create free influence: every Sybil needs its own capital at risk, and identities that cannot perform the work lose their bonds. A nebula of cheap accounts may reach the zenith of registration, but it cannot harvest rewards without paying this cost; an orchard of verified work grows only as fast as the attacker can fund and sustain real performance.
